subject: Post-demo: API identity patterns, tool-calling constraints, and embedding/reranker access
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chang <alex@finlytics.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: API identity patterns, tool-calling constraints, and embedding/reranker access

Alex / Emily — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a concrete plan for the architecture work we discussed (auth, SDK onboarding, routing, and embedding/reranker access controls).

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Finlytics wants a quick POC to validate latency and secure access for: (a) SDK-based client usage (web + server-side), (b) tool-calling/structured outputs with an external connector, and (c) embeddings + reranker pipeline for search relevance.
- Security constraints: Finlytics requires no long-lived plaintext keys stored in their customer vault, auditability for each token use, and automated rotation with minimal developer friction.
- Compliance: logs must include token identity and model variant; SOC2 evidence will be requested in a second wave.

Proposed identity pattern options (high-level):
1) Short-lived JWTs issued by Finlytics IdP + Redwood service account binding
   - Flow: Finlytics creates short-lived JWT (signed with their private key) including sub/org claims -> Redwood validates on intake with cached JWKS -> exchange for a short-lived Redwood bearer token (1 hour).
   - Pros: No permanent secret transfer; aligns to your existing IdP; good auditability.
   - Cons: Requires JWKS rotation sync; need to document ephemeral token exchange endpoint.

2) Ephemeral SDK API keys (per-developer/project) minted via an onboarding API
   - Flow: Admin calls Redwood onboarding endpoint with OIDC assertion -> Redwood mints ephemeral API key with attached scopes and TTL; key stored in Finlytics vault if desired.
   - Pros: Very easy for SDKs, minimal code changes for client teams.
   - Cons: Additional minting service and stricter rate limits; edge for browser usage needs extra protection (PKCE / browser token broker).

3) Service accounts + short-lived signed exchange (recommended for server-side workloads)
   - Flow: Create a Redwood service account for Finlytics (scoped to projects/models) -> service account credentials stored in Finlytics KMS -> applications request signed short-lived exchange tokens from Finlytics backend to call Redwood.
   - Pros: Clear separation of duties, easy to revoke at service-account level.

Security controls we should surface in the POC:
- Token TTL defaults: 1 hour (production), 15m (high-risk endpoints like tool-calling).
- Rotation: automated JWKS refresh with monitoring; recommended key rotation cadence 90 days for signing keys, ephemeral issuance for API tokens.
- Audit events: token_issued, token_exchanged, request_authenticated (include model, route, token_id).
- Scope-based access: embeddings-only vs generation vs tool-calling; reranker pipeline requires embeddings_read + rerank_execute scopes.

Integration notes specific to tool-calling and structured outputs:
- Tool-calling endpoints must be annotated in the access control matrix; tool-call execution should require an additional scope and stricter TTL (recommended 15 minutes) to reduce blast radius.
- For external connectors (e.g., Finlytics' data source), recommend tokenized connector identity rather than reusing user tokens.

Embeddings / reranker considerations:
- Store embeddings with a reference to the issuing token_id for audit/tracing.
- Reranker service will accept a signed service-to-service token from Finlytics backend; avoid granting client-side tokens direct rerank_execute rights.

Attachments: I attached a 1-page options summary and a quick architecture diagram (redwood-auth-options.pdf, postcall-arch-diagram.png).

Suggested next steps (calls to action):
- Finlytics: confirm preferred IdP flow (JWT exchange vs onboarding API). Alex: can you confirm by EOD Wednesday?
- Redwood: we’ll produce a scoped POC plan (auth exchange endpoints, token TTLs, minimal SDK changes) and an initial estimate for engineering time. Karthik / Marissa, can you draft the POC plan and engineering estimate?
- Schedule: propose a 60-minute technical kickoff next week to lock integration details (suggest Tue 11/16 or Wed 11/17).

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: API identity patterns, tool-calling constraints, and embedding/reranker access

Soojin — appreciate the concise recap. A couple clarifications from our security team after we reviewed the recording: we prefer option (1) (short-lived JWTs from our IdP) because it fits our existing rotation and audit model. Two asks: 

1) Can Redwood support token binding so we can tie tokens to a specific client_id in case of leak?
2) For tool-calling, can we enforce a deny-by-default policy and opt-in explicit tool approvals per environment (dev/staging/prod)?

On the embeddings/reranker side: we need to ensure embeddings stored in Redwood or exported to our vector DB include only a reversible reference (no PII) and that retriever queries are logged with token_id.

We can confirm IdP flow by Wednesday EOD as requested. Regarding the kickoff, Tue 11/16 works for our infra lead — please send an invite.

Thanks,
Alex Chang
Head of Integrations | Finlytics
alex@finlytics.com

Looping back with an internal POC plan draft — keeping it minimal to unblock Finlytics engineering: 

POC scope (2 sprints):
- Sprint 1 (auth plumbing, token exchange):
  - Implement JWKS validator and exchange endpoint (redwood.ai/internal-exchange).
  - Support token binding metadata (client_id claim) and expose token_id in logs.
  - Add scope enforcement layer: embeddings_read, generation, tool_call.
  - Deliverable: demo token exchange and a sample server-side call with scopes.

- Sprint 2 (SDK onboarding, tool-call gating, embeddings hygiene):
  - Ephemeral SDK key minting path for developer convenience (admin-onboard + OIDC assertion).
  - Tool-calling deny-by-default switch and environment-level approvals in Console.
  - Embedding pipeline: attach token_id and redaction marker for PII policy; log retriever queries with token_id.
  - Deliverable: end-to-end demo: server app exchanges JWT -> calls generation and embeddings endpoints; Console shows token usage and approved tools.

Owners / rough estimate:
- Karthik: backend token exchange, JWKS/validator, logging hooks (3w).
- Marissa: SDK changes + onboarding API, Console changes for tool approvals (3w).
- Soojin: integration test plan + runbook for Finlytics (1w).

I'll turn this into a short Confluence/POC doc and attach to the HubSpot deal. Assuming Alex confirms IdP path on Wednesday we can lock sprint 1 scope and schedule the 11/16 kickoff.

-Karthik
